mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stop falling and turn up from their recent lows, weekday trip chaining should increase discretionary shopping visits and lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise week-on-week after at least one week below their t-1w levels
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was -8.0 at t-1w and 2.3 at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed negative around -10 to -11
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean by week 4, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising RESIDENTIAL share signals people spending more time at home, which directly suppresses shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained elevated at 6.3, 6.0, 8.0, and 7.1 across the four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays at or above its current elevated range but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean within 2 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility drops sharply below its recent level, it marks broader crowding avoidance and reduced out-of-home leisure, which should depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40 and remains there for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -35.1 and -36.3 to -40.0 and -43.6
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below -40 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean over the following month, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rebound in TRANSIT reflects localized essential trips rather than broad citywide activity, so RETAIL_REC will stay flat or weaken over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above TRANSIT by at least 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive while TRANSIT remained negative
failure_condition: If the GROCERY_PHARM-TRANSIT gap stays above 15 points yet RETAIL_REC rises in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates fewer commuting-linked shopping opportunities, which should lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed negative while WORKPLACES fell to -8.0 at t-1w
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 2 weeks, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises above its recent average while PARKS remains deeply negative, the pattern is consistent with stay-at-home substitution that suppresses discretionary retail visits over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 7 while PARKS stays below -40

failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 7 and PARKS remains below -40 but RETAIL_REC does not weaken relative to the prior 4-week mean by week 4, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS accompanied by stable or falling TRANSIT signals weather- or season-driven reduction in outside activity, which should reduce RETAIL_REC after roughly four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined steadily across the snapshot while TRANSIT stayed negative
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below its recent average for a month but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover first and RESIDENTIAL simultaneously softens, the implied return-to-office pattern increases lunch and after-work shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC within two to four weeks.
